data.summary:
**Most likely explanation: Wildfire or burn scar.**

Burn severity (dNBR) on the ground that was vegetated before: dnbr_burnable was 0.2477 dNBR (0.1 to 0.27 dNBR) [[r_b0d42e79a649efd7#mean_delta]].

Share of the vegetated ground where NBR fell: nbr_loss_fraction_burnable was 0.763 of clear pixels (>= 0.5 of clear pixels) [[r_b0d42e79a649efd7#decreased_pct]].

Land cover of the area (ESA WorldCover 2021): cropland_pct was 0 % cropland (< 10 % cropland) [[r_ca788d725c5b1da0#cropland_pct]].

A vision model looks at the true-colour scene could not be measured: the picture could not be classified (model disabled (--no-llm)).

Limits: Active-fire detections are near real time (the last days); they cannot confirm a fire in an older window. dNBR compares two single Sentinel-2 scenes and is averaged over the pixels that were vegetated before the event (NBR 0.15 or more); a fire smaller than that cover is still diluted. In built-up areas a burn is measured only on the trees, grass and gardens among the buildings. Burnt roofs and walls are not measured: the investigator has no building-damage measure, and if too little of the area was vegetated (under 30 pixels) the burn items are reported as not measurable rather than as zero. The historical burned-area products in the registry (MODIS MCD64A1 at 500 m, Copernicus CLMS at 300 m) are not used: they cannot be read in-app without credentials and are coarse for a drawn area of a few kilometres. Burn scars separate wildfire from agricultural burning only by extent and land cover, which are indirect.
